intent: Make the Python tests workflow actually trigger when the dependency list changes, so a requirements fix cannot silently skip the workflow it is meant to repair.
scope: Non-goal: changing the symlink layout, which the repo documents deliberately
changes: Added meta/requirements.txt alongside requirements.txt in both path filters. The root file is a symlink into meta/, and GitHub matches filters against the path as git records it, so editing the real file did not match the symlink's name.

verification.command: Observed on commit 32de2215, which changed meta/requirements.txt
verification.evidence: Dependency Graph, Shell tests and Pre-commit checks all ran; Python tests did NOT trigger at all, leaving the last Python tests result on the older red commit 5ba2cbd4
YAML valid; both the push and pull_request filter lists were patched (2 occurrences)
Dispatched run 32645075080 to confirm the dependency fix itself, since the filter bug prevented an automatic run

risks: The other root symlinks (pyproject.toml, run.sh, lint_python.sh, .fvmrc) are not referenced by any workflow path filter today, so they carry the same latent trap if one is ever added.
rollback: Remove the meta/requirements.txt lines from both filters.
After rollback, a change to meta/requirements.txt will once again skip this workflow.
